name: wan-s1-ports
description: Plan 11.3's `conn 4` port-range run: the S1 production profile with the tunnel spread over UDP 29910-29913 (kcptun multiport) instead of one port, on a real path. S1 already dials `conn 4`, so this is the same four sessions over four ports rather than four over one — the arrangement a user picks when a middlebox rate-limits per flow, and the one place a real path can show whether both implementations spread and reassemble across the range identically. All four pairs run (GG, RR, GR, RG), interleaved, because a port range is precisely where a mixed pair could differ: the spread over 29910-29913 is a client-side choice the server must follow, so GR and RG are the runs that prove the two implementations agree about which session belongs to which port. Ports: the tunnel is 29910+ and the pingpong target 22700, not the 29900/22600 defaults, so a WAN run cannot collide with a netns lab that is up on either host — the port check unions the host's listeners with both lab namespaces', and a detached soak owns the defaults inside kr-srv. The iperf3 bitrate cap (400 Mbit/s) is a guard rail, not the measurement: it is well above what a 1-vCPU box drives through a tunnel at this RTT, so it does not bind, but it stops an unexpectedly fast path from saturating lab-arm64's NIC (tools/lab/README.md, safety rule 6). A cap that binds makes every implementation report the cap, which is how the first attempt at this rung wasted half an hour: 60 Mbit/s, 60 Mbit/s, both directions, both implementations. Measured on the 131 ms rung before the campaign: a Go client on one vCPU drove 200 Mbit/s up (cap-bound) and 145 Mbit/s down at a load average of 0.93, so the real limit is the client's single core, not the path — the cap is set above that so it never becomes the thing being compared. The reverse test starts 95 s after the forward one, not 70: one `iperf3 -s` serves both, and at 131 ms a finished forward test is still draining the tunnel's smux buffers when the next one dials — which is exactly how the first S2 session lost its last three runs to `the server is busy running a test`.
